critique.problem: The title says that center-based rehab caused better attendance, but the chart only compares attendance percentages and does not establish causation.
critique.repair: Use a descriptive title 'Rehabilitation attendance by program and quarter'.

critique.problem: The y-axis starts near 76%, which visually exaggerates the small differences in attendance between programs.
critique.repair: Start the bar-chart y-axis at 0% with ax.set_ylim(0, 100).

critique.problem: The y-axis has no label, so readers may confuse the values with percentages or raw counts.
Only red versus green separates the seasons, and the bars use the same hatch pattern; colorblind readers may not be able to tell them apart.
critique.repair: 'Use colorblind-safe colors plus a different hatch or direct label for each program.

critique.problem: Thick black edges, a heavy grid, and the same hatch on every bar carry no data.
critique.repair: Drop the edges and grid and keep hatches only where they mark the season.

question: The chart should help compare the percentage of patients meeting the weekly exercise goal change across follow-up visits, and does the pattern differ between home-based and center-based programs.
audience: Rehabilitation coordinator, for making decisions about which programs to add follow-up support.
intended_claim: Center-based programs have higher percentage of patients meeting the weekly exercise goal than home-based programs.
y_measure: Percent of patients meeting the weekly exercise goal (%)
grain: One row and one plotted point represent one rehabilitation program at one follow-up visit.
text_alternative: Line chart showing follow-up visit number (visits 1 through 4) on the x-axis and the percentage of patients meeting the weekly exercise goal on the y-axis.For the Home-based program, from visit 1 to visit 4, goal attainment increases from 58% to 70%. For the Center-based program, it increases from 57% to 79%.At visit 4, the Center-based program is 9 percentage points higher than the Home-based program, 79% versus 70%This difference is descriptive, patients were not randomized for they chose their program, so the gap does not show that one program causes more exercise.Each percentage covers only the patients seen at that visit, about 45 per program, so a 9-point gap could also come from chance or from who returned.
